title: Days Until Warmer
statement: temps[i] is the temperature on day i. For each day, return how many days you have to wait until a strictly warmer day. If no warmer day ever comes, the answer for that day is 0.

examples.explanation: Day 2 (75) waits 4 days for 76 on day 6.

tests.purpose: an equal temperature is not warmer
catches O(n^2): nobody ever finds a warmer day

optimal.approach_name: monotonic decreasing stack of day indices

acceptable_suboptimal.note: Scanning forward from every day is a fine first idea.

hint_ladder.hint: When you reach a warm day, which earlier days does it answer all at once?
A stack can hold the days that are still waiting for a warmer day.
Keep the waiting days in a stack whose temperatures decrease from bottom to top. A new warmer day settles every colder waiting day, starting from the top.
Push day indices. For each new day, while the day on top is colder, pop it and set its answer to the difference of the indices. Then push the new day.

common_mistakes.description: Treating an equal temperature as warmer (<= instead of <).
Leaving days that never get a warmer day as -1 instead of 0.
Pushing temperatures instead of day indices, then guessing the day with temps.index(), which breaks on repeated temperatures.
